key_insight: MedRLM proposes a recursive, multimodal clinical reasoning framework that iteratively inspects text, images, sensor data, and guidelines instead of relying on one-shot prompting.
clinical_relevance: It is designed to support more auditable decision support for long, complex patient cases, including screening and referral decisions across community-to-tertiary care settings.
method: Coordinates specialized agents for EHR, radiology, sensor signals, guideline retrieval, uncertainty auditing, and referral planning.
Uses a Clinical Evidence Graph Memory to link patient observations with evidence, biomarkers, and referral criteria.
Triggers deeper reasoning when abnormal sensor patterns or low-confidence findings are detected.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a planned evaluation on public and credentialed datasets spanning EHR, radiology, ECG, ICU time series, and referral-proxy outcomes.
watch_item: The approach may be difficult to deploy safely without strong data integration, calibration, and clinical validation across sites and workflows.
paper_title: MedRLM: Recursive Multimodal Health Intelligence for Long-Context Clinical Reasoning, Sensor-Guided Screening, Evidence-Grounded Decision Support, and Community-to-Tertiary Referral Optimization
